chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Taslim (saying 'Assalamu Alaikum'), what is it? He said, 'It is permission.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: The act of saying 'Assalamu Alaikum' at the beginning of prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling of Taslim in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the legal status of the initial *Taslim* as 'permission' (*idhn*), indicating that it serves as the formal conclusion of the prayer's obligatory acts. This definition underscores the transition from the state of prayer (*salah*) to the state of freedom (*halal*), where the worshiper is no longer bound by the specific restrictions of the prayer ritual. This interpretation is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the precise moment when the prayer is considered complete and valid.
